title: Backend mid scenario zero downtime migration
topic: Backend mid scenario zero downtime migration
question: You need to rename a column that's actively read and written by a live service handling continuous traffic, with no maintenance window. How do you do it safely?
idealAnswer:
Rejects the naive single-step rename, since a rolling deploy means old and new application code run simultaneously against the same database for a period, and either version would break if the column were renamed atomically

Proposes an expand-and-contract (multi-step) approach: first add the new column alongside the old one, deploy code that writes to both, backfill existing rows, then deploy code that reads from the new column, and only drop the old column once nothing references it

Explains why each step needs to be independently safe and backward-compatible, so the deploy can proceed instance by instance without any window where some instances break

Considers backfilling large tables carefully, e.g. in batches, to avoid a single long-running migration that locks the table or overloads the database

Mentions verifying (e.g. via logging or a temporary check) that nothing is still reading the old column before actually dropping it, rather than assuming the code changes were complete
